Guidance: Use energy-efficient LED lighting and switch off lights in unoccupied rooms.
Optimize HVAC operating schedules according to room occupancy and avoid unnecessary cooling.
Switch off computers laboratory equipment and other high-load devices when they are not required.
Monitor electricity consumption regularly to identify unusual increases and investigate high-consumption areas.
Inspect taps pipelines storage tanks and fixtures regularly to identify leaks and prevent water loss.
Avoid unnecessary water use and encourage responsible consumption across campus facilities.
Investigate sudden increases in water consumption because they may indicate leakage overflow or abnormal usage.
Where suitable use rainwater harvesting and water reuse practices to reduce dependence on fresh water.
Separate recyclable organic and other waste at the point of disposal using clearly labelled bins.
Reduce single-use materials and avoid unnecessary consumption to minimize waste generation.
Increase recycling of paper plastic metal and other recoverable materials through appropriate collection systems.
Monitor waste generation by building or area to identify locations with unusually high waste production.
Prefer digital forms online submissions and electronic documentation whenever practical.
Avoid unnecessary printing and use double-sided printing when physical documents are required.
Track paper consumption over time and identify departments or buildings with unusually high usage.
Prefer durable reusable and resource-efficient products when purchasing campus supplies and equipment.
Use consumption data and anomaly detection to identify unusual resource patterns and prioritize corrective actions.
Conduct periodic resource-use audits to evaluate performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
Provide sustainability awareness activities so students and staff understand how everyday actions affect resource consumption.
AI recommendations should be treated as decision-support information and verified by responsible campus personnel before action.
Avoid collecting unnecessary personal information when using campus resource data and restrict access to appropriate personnel.
Explain important AI findings using understandable evidence such as observed usage baseline values and deviation percentages.
Human staff should review significant alerts before making operational decisions based on AI recommendations.
Prioritize practical actions that reduce unnecessary resource consumption while maintaining essential campus services.
